title: Burst reserve sizing & token COGS by region - playbook
body:
Purpose:
This working spreadsheet outlines a proposed approach for sizing short-term reserved capacity (microburst reserves) for the Hosted API and mapping per-token COGS and margin by model family and region. Aim: reduce tail latency SLA violations during short bursts while keeping unit-economics transparent and minimizing wasted committed capacity.

Status: draft — exploratory formulas, test cohorts defined, open questions at the end.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Current hosted unit-econ workbooks focus on average token costs and steady-state capacity. That underweights the economic impact of short, high-QPS bursts (customer spikes, product launches) that force either degraded latency or emergency overprovisioning. This playbook models: 1) a small regional reserve pool sized to cover short bursts (30s-5m) by converting expected burst QPS into GPU-seconds; 2) a marginal per-token surcharge allocation to reserve costs ("burst amortization"); 3) scenario sensitivity across regions (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1) and model families (small: rwd-open-3B, mid: rwd-opt-13B, large: rwd-quant-70B). Recommendations: (a) pilot dynamic reserve pools in US-W and EU-W with 5–8% effective amortization on high-latency-sensitive routes; (b) adopt mix of quantized mid-tier models for burst fallback to reduce reserve sizing and COGS.

Sheet layout (how to reproduce quickly):
- Tab A: assumptions (strings + numbers)
  - region
  - model_family
  - avg_tokens_per_request (T)
  - avg_latency_ms (L)
  - baseline_qps_95 (Q95)
  - burst_qps_target (QB) — e.g., 2x Q95 or measured peak events
  - burst_duration_s (D) — 30, 60, 300
  - gpu_tokens_per_sec (G) by model (measured on our runtime)
  - gpu_cost_per_minute_region (C)
- Tab B: reserve sizing calculations (per region / model family)
  - burst_tokens = QB * D * T
  - required_gpu_seconds = burst_tokens / (G)
  - reserve_gpu_minutes = ceil(required_gpu_seconds / 60 * safety_factor)
  - reserve_monthly_cost = reserve_gpu_minutes * C * 60 * (avg_burst_events_per_month)
- Tab C: amortized per-token surcharge
  - amortized_cost_per_token = reserve_monthly_cost / (monthly_tokens_for_routes_guarded)
  - effective_cogs_per_token = baseline_token_cogs + amortized_cost_per_token
  - margin_impact_pct = (list_price_per_token - effective_cogs_per_token) / list_price_per_token

Key formulas (Excel-friendly):
- Burst tokens (cell): =QB * D * T
- Required GPU seconds: =burst_tokens / G
- Reserve GPU minutes (rounded up): =CEILING(required_gpu_seconds / 60 * safety_factor, 1)
- Reserve monthly cost: =reserve_gpu_minutes * C * avg_burst_events_per_month
- Amortized cost per token: =reserve_monthly_cost / monthly_tokens_for_routes_guarded

Assumptions (initial values used for pilot tests):
- regions: us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1
- model families and G (gpu_tokens_per_sec):
  - rwd-open-3B: 2,200 tokens/sec/GPU (fp16)
  - rwd-opt-13B: 680 tokens/sec/GPU (fp16)
  - rwd-quant-70B: 120 tokens/sec/GPU (int8)
- gpu_cost_per_minute_region (C):
  - us-west1: $0.75 / GPU-minute (on-demand equivalent)
  - eu-west1: $0.84 / GPU-minute
  - ap-southeast1: $0.95 / GPU-minute
- avg_tokens_per_request (T): 120
- avg_burst_events_per_month: 8 (assume 8 short bursts/month)
- safety_factor: 1.15 (15% headroom for variance)

Worked example (US-W, rwd-opt-13B, 60s burst, QB = 2x Q95 where Q95=100 qps so QB=200):
- burst_tokens = 200 qps * 60 s * 120 tokens = 1,440,000 tokens
- required_gpu_seconds = 1,440,000 / 680 = 2117.65 s (~35.3 minutes)
- reserve_gpu_minutes = CEILING(35.3 / 60 * 1.15, 1) = CEILING(0.676 * 1.15, 1) -> compute differently: reserve minutes approx = CEILING(35.3 / 60 * 1.15 / 1, 1) = CEILING(0.676 * 1.15,1) = 1 minute (this highlights that single-minute buckets are coarse; instead we should express reserve in GPU-minutes directly)
Alternative compute (reserve GPU-minutes = required_gpu_seconds/60 * safety_factor = 35.3/60*1.15 = 0.676 -> round up to 1 GPU-minute per burst).
- reserve_monthly_cost = 1 GPU-minute * $0.75 * 8 = $6.00/month (this small number is because burst durations are short; the cost becomes material with heavier bursts or many routes guarded)
- monthly_tokens_for_routes_guarded (assume 20M tokens/month) -> amortized = $6 / 20,000,000 = $0.0000003 per token -> negligible in this example.

Sensitivity note: for larger models (rwd-quant-70B) required_gpu_seconds grows sharply and reserve costs can dominate. Example same burst for 70B: required_gpu_seconds = 1,440,000 / 120 = 12,000s -> 200 GPU-minutes -> reserve_monthly_cost = 200 * $0.75 * 8 = $1,200/month -> amortized per token = $1,200 / 20,000,000 = $0.00006 (6e-05) per token.

Interpretation & heuristics:
- Short bursts measured in seconds often map to small reserve-minute charges when using per-minute GPU billing. However, high-token requests or large models escalate required GPU-time and change the calculus.
- For latency-sensitive routes, maintain a small reserve sized for 1–3x observed Q95 for 60–300s bursts; for cost-sensitive routes use fallback routes that switch to quantized or smaller model families during burst events.
- Use per-route tagging in the router so that only a subset of traffic is granted burst protection (e.g., checkout flows, modal chat windows).

Operational playbook (pilot):
1) Instrument: add per-route Q95/Q99 and peak-burst detection hook (SLO-team / infra). (owner: Marcus) — 2 weeks
2) Simulate: generate synthetic bursts against canary region using representative prompt mixes and measure G (gpu_tokens_per_sec) and latency degradation curves. (owner: Zara) — 1 week
3) Size: run the sheet across region/model families and produce reserve recommendations (owner: Priya) — 3 days
4) Implement reserve pools (Dedicated-style ephemeral pools) for 2 regions; integrate router fallback policies (owner: Ethan) — 3 weeks
5) Measure & iterate: track amortized cost per token and SLA events, adjust safety_factor and guarded routes after 2 months. (owner: Priya + Marcus)

Routing & fallback strategy examples:
- Primary: rwd-opt-13B in region; Reserve: 1–2 GPU-minutes per expected burst; Fallback policy: if queue > 500ms or reserve not available, route to rwd-open-3B with warmed KV cache.
- Aggressive-cost: Primary: rwd-quant-70B (heavy), Reserve: prefer quantized variant or a mid-size fallback to minimize reserve sizing.

Cost allocation model thoughts:
- Option A (conservative): amortize reserve entirely across all tokens for the customer who triggered protected route(s).
- Option B (shared pool): amortize across all customers using that route category in region (better smoothing but hides behavioral cost signals).
- Option C (surcharge): expose explicit latency-burst surcharge for enterprise customers who require reserved burst protection (transparent but friction).

Spreadsheet tabs to export to Finance (format suggestions):
- Region-model-reserve-summary.csv: columns: region, model_family, burst_qps, burst_dur_s, reserve_gpu_minutes_per_burst, monthly_cost, amortized_cost_per_token, scenario_tag
- Per-route-impact.csv: route_id, protected_flag, monthly_tokens, expected_amortized_per_token, price_delta_pct

Open questions / risks:
- Billing granularity: our cloud provider billing rounding can make per-burst minute-level math noisy. Need to baseline real billing logs.
- Frequency of bursts: if bursts are >20/month, reserve amortization increases linearly and may justify different contract/Reserved instances.
- Multi-region overflow: how to account for cross-region routing (cheaper region serving bursts for other regions) given egress and latency tradeoffs.
- Long-tail rare events: 1-in-1000 events (huge spikes) are not cost-effective to reserve for; need autoscaling fallback policies and graceful degradation.

Action items (short list):
- [ ] Marcus: add Q95/Q99 and burst detector metrics to per-route dashboards (due 2026-02-24)
- [ ] Zara: run synthetic-burst sim and report GPU-token throughput table (due 2026-02-28)
- [ ] Priya: finalize pilot sizing sheet and produce CSV exports for finance (due 2026-03-05)
- [ ] Ethan: prototype router policy for guarded routes + fallback chain (due 2026-03-15)

Notes to self / rough bits:
- This sheet intentionally uses round numbers; when we plug telemetry make all rates time-windowed (rolling 1h Q95) and include weekday vs weekend splits.
- Consider coupling with cost-optimization signals from Optimize: if quantization can reduce GPU_seconds by 40% for a route, reserve pool sizing can shrink by same factor.
- Potentially add a separate tab for enterprise contracted customers where we show "breach insurance" pricing (fixed monthly fee to cover X bursts).

References and quick links:
- Runtime perf notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1132
- Related token econ workbooks (internal): Confluence: Token Econ Playbook (linked above)

End of draft.

-- Priya
